content:
A few weeks ago, JPMorgan set a 2027 December price target of $345 for Apple stock. After yesterday's quarterly results, the investment bank has slightly revised its outlook. Here are the details.

JPMorgan Lowers Apple Price Target

According to AppleInsider, JPMorgan has raised its price target on Apple stock from $345 to $350.

The AppleInsider report reads:

JPMorgan's revision comes after Apple yesterday reported quarterly results and warned that memory shortages will significantly worsen supply constraints in the September quarter — particularly for iPhone, iPad and Mac. These three business segments typically account for around 64% of Apple's fourth fiscal quarter revenue.

In yesterday's earnings report, Apple also disclosed a 5% decline in iPad revenue and pointed to a slowdown in services growth, partly due to softer App Store gaming revenue, regulatory changes in certain countries, and its ongoing legal dispute with Epic Games — a dispute that prevents Apple from collecting commissions on purchases made by US users via external links.

Apple's stock opened down 8.6% today, currently trading at $301.41, a 9.6% drop from yesterday's close. The sharp market reaction comes just days after Apple briefly surpassed the $5 trillion market capitalisation mark, overtaking Nvidia to become the world's most valuable company. Apple's stock is up 11% year-to-date.
